items.summary: TypeScriptとは？ TypeScript は JavaScript に静的型付けを追加した言語で、Microsoft が開発しています。JavaScript のスーパーセットであるため、既存の JavaScript のコードをそのまま活かしながら、型の恩恵を受けられるのが特徴です。 TypeScriptでは、型を定義したり、型を変数のように扱ったり、型同士を組み合わせたりできるため、最初は少し難しく感じるかもしれません。しかし、これらの機能を理解することで、より安全で保守性の高いコードを書くことができます。 本記事では、私が実務で特によく使用した以下の機能を、具体例を交えなが...
items.titleJa: 【TypeScript入門】実務でよく使う機能を徹底解説｜Generics・keyof・typeof・as const
items.summaryJa:
TypeScriptはJavaScriptに静的型付けを追加するスーパーセットで、実務では型エラーの検出やエディタの支援を強化する点が特に重宝されます。本文は、型定義やオプショナルプロパティ、typeof・keyof・as constの組み合わせによるバリデーション、そしてジェネリクスの使い方と活用例を具体的に解説しています。

型定義を使うとデータ構造を明示でき、例として { id: number; name: string; email?: string } のように必須/オプショナルを表現できます。typeofで値から型を生成し、keyofで型からキーのUnion型を作る仕組みや、as const によるリテラル型の固定と組み合わせたバリデーションの考え方も紹介されています。ジェネリクスでは、関数や関数群を複数の型で再利用可能にする方法を、単一の型パラメータや複数の型パラメータを使う例とともに解説しており、用途としてはデータ取得関数や結合処理などが挙げられます。以上を通じて、型安全性を保ちながら柔軟で再利用性の高いコードを書く考え方が説明されています。

items.title: shadcn のサイドメニュー、リロードで困った話
items.summary: 環境 Next.js 16（App Router / Turbopack） React 19 shadcn/ui（base-nova registry） Biome 起きたこと shadcn ベースのサイドバーで開閉状態を localStorage に保存していた。サイドバーのデフォルトは展開（開いた）状態だ。ユーザーが閉じた状態でリロードすると、一瞬デフォルトの展開状態が見えてからパッと閉じる。いわゆる FOUC が起きた。 なぜ起きるか localStorage はブラウザでしか読めない。Next.js の SSR はサーバー側で HTML を生成するので、local...
items.titleJa: shadcn のサイドメニュー、リロードで困った話
items.summaryJa: サイドバーの開閉状態を localStorage で管理していたが、SSR なので初回HTMLはサーバー側で localStorage の値を読めず、開いた状態が出力されてしまい、ブラウザで実行後に値を切り替えることでチラつき（FOUC）が発生していた。解決策として cookie を用いた Persisted State を採用し、サーバー側で cookie を読み取って初期値を決定することで SSR 時点から正しい幅のHTMLを生成でき、チラつきを抑制できることを説明している。実装はクライアント側で cookie に保存し、サーバー側の layout.tsx で next/headers の cookies() で読み取り、AppShell に defaultSidebarOpen を渡す形。補足として SPA にはこの方法は適用できず、blocking script や beforeInteractive の組み合わせでは初期描画の保証が難しい点も指摘している。

items.title: How Speechify serves 500,000 dynamic pages to 60 million users on Vercel
items.summary: Speechify on Vercel 500,000+ pages served across 40+ languages Cut costs 50% by auto-scaling with Fluid compute Zero user impact on bad deploys with Instant Rollbacks Speechify started as a tool for people with dyslexia. Cliff Weitzman, Founder & CEO, built it because reading was challenging and audio made it much easier. That initial use case led Speechify to tens of millions of users and an Apple Design Award for inclusion. The product has since grown into something much larger: an AI work platform where 60 million people listen to documents, delegate tasks to agents, and complete work entirely through voice. But the journey wasn't easy. Early on, they got hacked, and for half a day, every visitor was redirected to a casino website. After that, Denis Chernobai, Head of Growth Engineering, knew it was time to re-evaluate their infrastructure stack. He decided to rebuild from scratch on Next.js and Vercel, and they ended up serving 40 times more pages, reaching a global audience three times larger, and achieving a 50% cost reduction. Since migrating to Vercel, Speechify has maintained 99.99% uptime and hasn't had a single security incident. The cost of serving 500,000 dynamic pages Speechify's website is its primary growth engine, with 10,000 base pages translated into 40+ languages across onboarding funnels, localized landing pages, and pricing experiments that change constantly. Static generation isn't an option because the content changes too frequently. But serving everything dynamically means every visitor is a potential database read, which compounds fast at hundreds of thousands of visits every day. Vercel's Data Cache, ISR, and Next.js Cache Components resolve both problems at once. Pages render dynamically on first visit, cache immediately, and serve from the closest point of presence until something changes. The result is a global growth engine that scales without the infrastructure costs scaling with it. The risk of shipping to 60 million users Instant Rollbacks: ship fast, fix faster Speechify's growth team ships constantly. New funnels and A/B experiments are deployed every few days to a user base of millions who expect everything to work. At that scale, a bad release isn't a bug for developers to fix. It's a revenue problem that can show up before anyone has time to react. Before Vercel, a bad release meant scrambling to patch it before it became an incident. That shift from deploying with dread to deploying with confidence is what enables a small growth team to operate at a speed that would otherwise require a much larger team. The cost of moving slower than the market Next.js on Vercel: from code to global delivery When AI moves this fast, you need to constantly ship to stay competitive, and capabilities evolve rapidly, often every few weeks. "We see new voice functionality and agents emerging that didn't exist just last month," said Rohan Pavuluri, Speechify's Chief Business Officer. Each week that an idea remains unimplemented is a week someone else might bring it to life first. With Next.js on Vercel, the only hurdle to turning an idea into reality is the code itself. Speechify ships on Next.js with continuous deployments. The growth team doesn't have a dedicated platform engineering function and doesn't need one. Security patches apply automatically, infrastructure scales to demand with Fluid compute , and there's no deployment pipeline to maintain. What's next Speechify is expanding into new international markets and shipping new AI capabilities to millions of users. Most recently, they launched SpeechifyAI , a developer platform bringing the same voice technology behind their consumer success to builders via API, and its flagship Simba 3.2 model ranks number one on the Artificial Analysis text-to-speech leaderboard as of July 2026. As the product grows and the user base expands, Vercel is scaling with it, from cached pages to continuous deployments on a platform that lets their small, focused engineering team compete with companies ten times their size.
